25477.description:
We are seeking a proactive and capable
HR Executive
to manage and support the HR function for our operations in
Papua New Guinea
to be based at
Port Moresby
. This role will be responsible for end-to-end HR operations, providing sound HR advice, and ensuring compliance with PNG labour laws and regulations.
Key Responsibilities
Manage the HR Department and oversee day-to-day HR and payroll operations.
Provide HR advice and guidance to management and employees on policies, procedures, and people matters.
Interpret and apply PNG labour laws, employment legislation, and statutory requirements, ensuring organisational compliance.
Support the full employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, confirmations, transfers, and exits.
Prepare, issue, and maintain employment contracts, HR documentation, and employee records.
Coordinate and support recruitment activities, including job postings, shortlisting, interviews, and offer documentation.
Support payroll administration by ensuring accurate HR data, attendance, and leave records.
Manage leave, benefits, and statutory entitlements in line with PNG requirements.
Handle employee relations matters, including grievances, disciplinary actions, and performance issues, in line with company policy and labour laws.
Support and administer performance management and KPI processes.
Coordinate training and development initiatives and maintain training records.
Prepare HR reports and provide insights and recommendations to management.
Key Requirements
Degree or Diploma in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years’ experience in an HR generalist or HR executive role, preferably managing HR operations independently.
Strong knowledge and practical experience in PNG labour laws and employment regulations.
Proven ability to provide HR advisory support and interpret employment legislation.
High level of integrity and ability to handle sensitive matters with confidentiality.
Strong leadership, organisational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Proficiency in MS Office and HR/payroll systems.
How to apply:
If you meet the above criteria, please send your application and CV with Subject"
HR Executive - PNG"
to Email:

25458.description:
PNG Air, renowned for its extensive network covering over 26 destinations throughout Papua New Guinea, operates the largest fleet of ATR 72-600 series aircraft in the region. As the Airline of Choice, we're committed to delivering a world-class experience with competitive fares, unparalleled cargo rates, and a focus on safety and on-time performance for our valued customers and stakeholders.
ACCOUNTS PAYABLE SUPERVISOR
We are pleased to announce an open vacancy now exists in our Finance Department for a qualified and experienced Accounts Payable Supervisor.
Based in Port Moresby this position will report to Accounts Payable Manager. This role will coordinate, lead and supervise the effective management of all company’s creditor’s accounts and related duties in accordance with the company’s operational and business requirements, providing the required support to the Accounts Payable Manager, to meet all line departments/divisions operational and administrative needs.
The AP Supervisor will be responsible for the following key responsibilities:
Co-ordinate with relevant departments/divisions to ensure a smooth transition/flow of documents between them and the finance/accounts payable section
Ensure correct procedures (SOP) are followed before any request for payment is done
Task to complete monthly reports within the set dead line as required
Checking and posting of creditors data entry batches and payment
Review of creditor’s reconciliations, statement of account versus the creditors’ age payable listing
Liaising with other department/division regarding queries
Preparation of ad hoc reports as required by the Accounts Payable Manager and or the Manager-Financial Planning & Analysis
Provide training to junior level staff
Other duties as assigned as requested by Finance Management team
QUALIFICATION/EXPERIENCE
Tertiary qualified with an appropriate Accounting back ground.
Experience in Accounts Payable functions and processes.
Display a sound understanding of Accounts Payables objectives and plans including operating systems used in the aviation industry.
The ability to proactively provide supervision employing systems and processes and procedures and to operate effectively meeting the Accounts Payables requirements.
Ability to provide guidance to the junior level staff within Accounts Payable.
Be hard working, trustworthy and results oriented/focused.
Proficient in MS Software (MS Word, MS Excel).
Knowledgeable in Accpac Software (desirable but not required)
3 years experiences supervising an AP team.
If you feel you meet our requirements and are interested, we would like to hear from you. Send your application in only one PDF file to:
[email protected]
Applications close:
Friday 02nd January 2026
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted
We are an equal opportunity employer.
Apply

25440.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who maybe looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the
Faith & Development Coordinator
role to be based in
Port Moresby, National Capital District.
MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Project Leadership & Management
Oversee day-to-day operations of WVPNG Faith & Development projects and internal initiatives to ensure timely and effective implementation.
Ensure adherence to project norms, policies, and quality standards.
Monitor progress against objectives and adjust plans as needed.
Conduct annual assessments, develop action plans, and report quarterly on progress.
Staff Spiritual Formation & Capacity Building
Work with People & Culture and Senior Management to build staff capacity and contribute to an ethos aligned with World Vision’s Vision, Mission, Core Values, Guiding Principles, and Policies.
Develop and implement program strategies for staff spiritual nurture and holistic formation relating to leadership and capacity building.
Support staff to understand and demonstrate spiritual formation and leadership in their roles.
Strategic Leadership & Program Integration
Attend Senior Management Team meetings as required to provide corporate leadership for the Faith & Development program.
Contribute to ensuring ministry quality, integrity, and commitment to transformation in the lives of children and families.
Work with area program and national management to implement and evaluate the bi-annual Strategic Imperative 1 (SI1) Plan.
Strengthen integration of faith perspectives across all projects in alignment with SI1.
Stakeholder Engagement & Network Building
Mobilize and engage faith leaders, community leaders, and faith-based organizations to support shared ministry and child wellbeing targets.
Strengthen partnerships and resource sharing within the F&D space at all levels.
Organize and support network strengthening and relationship-building activities with faith leaders, churches, Christian agencies, and other faith-based organizations.
Reporting & Technical Support
Submit monthly, semi-annual, and annual reports to the National Director and Regional Faith & Development Advisor.
Highlight learning and progress through consistent reporting.
Provide technical support to Area Programs and portfolio managers on F&D integration in programming.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Minimum Educational level required: University Degree in Theology, project management (in related field is desired)
3 years of experience in Church or Christian ministry work
3 years of experience in project management
At least 5 years’ experience in international development work in an INGO setting
Good communication, networking and partnership skills with faith leaders is essential
Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. Demonstrated inter-personal skills in multicultural teams.
Demonstrated problem-solving and analytical skills, relevant for tasks related to research and strategy development.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel, email, and internet.
A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.
Interested applicants should submit the following documents all in one PDF file before;
Friday 2 January, 2026
,
(Midnight, PNG Time)
Expression of interest
Detailed CV
World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.
World Vision is committed to safeguarding all children and adults living where World Vision operates. We enforce a zero tolerance for any forms of  violence, abuse and exploitation against children or adults, either by employees or others affiliated with our work. We do not employ staff whose background is not aligned with our safe guarding practices. Employment is conditional upon successful completion of all mandatory background checks, including criminal record checks, where required.
We appreciate the time it takes to prepare your application. Please note that only short-listed candidates suitable for interviews will be contacted. If you do not hear from World Vision within
two (2) weeks
of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.
Apply

25430.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Superintendent Geotechnical, you will play a pivotal role in safeguarding operational excellence and safety across our mining operations. Entrusted with the oversight of geotechnical activities, you will lead the formulation and execution of strategic plans to enhance slope stability, manage advanced instrumentation and monitoring programs, and ensure the integrity of mine design parameters. Your expertise will be instrumental in driving continuous improvement, risk mitigation, and the delivery of timely, accurate geotechnical insights to support our operational teams. This leadership position offers the opportunity to collaborate with multidisciplinary stakeholders, manage complex projects, and contribute meaningfully to Newmont’s commitment to responsible mining and sustainable growth.
As part of our team, you will
Lead the Mine Geotechnical team, fostering a collaborative and inclusive environment.
Develop, maintain, and execute strategic geotechnical plans to enhance slope stability and mine design.
Coordinate geotechnical and hydrological monitoring, data collection, and structural mapping.
Manage geotechnical project drilling, mapping, and laboratory tests.
Establish and maintain ground control management plans.
Provide timely, accurate geotechnical information to operations teams.
Identify and mitigate risks, ensuring compliance with safety standards.
Manage consultants, contractors, and project budgets.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Bachelor’s degree in Geotechnical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or related field.
Accreditation from the Institute of Engineers PNG Inc. (as part of work permit process).
Advanced proficiency in geotechnical engineering, hydrology, slope stability, and risk management.
Demonstrated experience with geotechnical instrumentation, including inclinometers, load cells, automated prisms and radar systems.
Experience in project and/or contract management.
Strong leadership, problem-solving, and collaboration skills.
Ability to work within established systems and adapt to changing conditions.
Commitment to safety and continuous improvement.
Your work environment
You’ll be part of a dynamic mining operation at our Lihir site, collaborating closely with various internal teams, as well as engaging with external consultants and contractors. The role combines office-based planning with field-based oversight, focusing on maintaining and optimizing existing infrastructure. This residential position offers the balance of a 5:2 roster, allowing you to contribute meaningfully at work while returning home to your family each evening. For the right candidate, FIFO (Fly-In Fly-Out) arrangements may be considered.
Beyond work, you’ll enjoy the best of tropical island living, with access to a vibrant range of social and recreational activities. Our comprehensive relocation program ensures a smooth transition into the local community, including cultural orientation, international-standard schooling (see more at
https://lisstm.com.au/)
, quality healthcare services, and household support.
Why Join Newmont
Be part of a global leader in mining, where your expertise drives operational excellence and safety. Newmont offers opportunities for professional growth, a supportive team culture, and the chance to make a meaningful impact on large-scale projects.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 02 January 2026 – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

Conduct Cranes and Rigging training needs analysis.
Deliver training using a range of methods, including online training, developing new programs and training plans that build workforce capability.
Supervise team members in executing operational and maintenance activities within the Asset Management area.

Coach, mentor, and support team development through regular feedback and structured training.
Ensure all operators perform isolations and issue safe work permits for maintenance activities in compliance with the site’s Permit to Work system.

Proven experience working with Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) and training frameworks.
Knowledge and application of adult learning principles to enhance training delivery and team development.
Demonstrated supervisory experience coordinating and training staff in technically challenging and remote work environments.
Experience in mineral processing environments involving large-scale fixed assets.
Extensive experience in relevant rigging and crane operating roles.
Ability to conduct audits and verify competencies effectively.
Advanced Rigging Licence and Crane Open Class (High Risk Licence) is essential.
Certificate IV in Training and Assessment is essential.
Proficiency in SAP and Microsoft Office Suite.

Previous expatriate experience working in remote locations.

A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
We offer a range of recreational activities including our on-site gym and basketball court. Paid members can access the Lihir Club which has a swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, restaurant/bar area and deck with amazing Pacific Ocean views! Our café and deli are available for take away coffees and snacks, as well as local and imported grocery items (inc. fresh fruit).

Opportunities for career growth, learning, and leadership development.

25415.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) has an exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for a suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the
Monitoring & Evaluation Officer
role to be based in
Arawa, Autonomous Region of Bougainville.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Program Design
Support MEAL Coordinator as requested (WVPNG, strategy, sectoral frameworks, overall, MEAL system set-up, ad-hoc requests)
Support the MEAL Coordinator in leading the proposal development process regarding MEAL input (logframe, budgeting for MEAL activities and staffing, MEAL narrative plan, etc.)
Develop project-specific MEAL frameworks in coordination with project staff.
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting
Develop methodologies, sampling plans, and tools for outcome and process monitoring studies, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, FGDs, KIIs, etc.
Plan, lead, and oversee the implementation of outcome monitoring studies for grants such as PIMs/PDMs, midline and endline studies, pre/post-tests, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (coordinate, follow up, and review the outcome monitoring methodology, tools, and reports for grants.
Lead assigned project-specific evaluations and baselines at the field level (development of ToR, selection and short-listing consultants, coordination with the consultant, review of design methodology and tools, review final reports, attend interpretation workshops, etc., if externally led; and conduct data analysis and report writing if internally led)
Implement field-level tasks for the outcome and process monitoring of the project, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, midline and end-line studies, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (training of casual workers, planning field data collection, coordination of data collection, supervising, facilitating, coding tools, developing datasets, data cleaning, analysis, reporting)
Provide support in training project staff and partners on reporting requirements, output level monitoring, and conduct regular training for project staff on data collection and data entry for pre-post-tests.
Conduct ITT verifications of projects in coordination with project staff each month and ensure project-level ITTs are updated with accurate data. Key findings are shared with the project team and management at the program review meetings.
Conduct regular project site visits and monitor partner & direct implementation against quality standards through scheduled visits, data quality audits, and spot checks.
Support the project teams in compiling regular quality project reports, including monthly (Monthly Management Report), Quarterly, mid-year, annual, and end-of-project reports.
Ensure that the project team and other stakeholders discuss and address critical MEAL findings and recommendations.
Accountability to Children & Communities
Assess community preferences and needs to inform the design of contextually appropriate accountability processes and share outcomes/results with communities, colleagues, and partners.
Implement the project accountability plan/design developed based on the community's preferences for providing information, consulting with communities, promoting participation, and collecting and acting on feedback and complaints.
Receive, process, and respond to feedback and complaints, and communicate progress to the children, communities, and stakeholders.
Implement the plan for sharing information based on community stakeholders' needs and preferences and adjust as needed. Collaborate with colleagues to gather relevant and accurate project information to be shared openly with communities, stakeholders, and partners.
Ensure that all feedback and complaints received from communities are promptly and accurately recorded/updated in the system, and that loops are closed within the timeline.
Sensitize community members about their right to information, consultation, participation, and providing feedback and complaints, while emphasizing their responsibility to support solutions.
Support investigation of allegations of irregularities, fraud, corruption, or other forms of misconduct by directly liaising with the affected communities, according to guidelines, and promptly, promoting trust and safety.
Engage community members in measuring the effectiveness of Accountability practices, providing recommendations for and addressing areas that need improvement in coordination with the accountability core team, and conducting other consultation activities that can support the design of new programmes.
Conduct exit interviews, observation, and reporting.
Research and Learning
Co-lead lessons learned events for the project with project managers and technical staff (preparation, facilitation, and report writing)
Implement any potential research studies at the field level (data collection, cleaning) - (based on WVPNG strategic priorities for Evidence Building)
Miscellaneous
Support WVPNG-wide PQ assignments such as assessments and program design, as assigned by the supervisor.
Attend internal and external meetings relevant to assigned projects
Attend internal and external training, workshops, events, etc.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
A BA Degree in international development, international relations, public health, nutrition, statistics, community development, or other relevant disciplines is required.
Minimum one to two years of experience in working in a relief or development NGO with a focus on MEAL processes
Experience in the design and implementation of MEAL systems, including qualitative and quantitative approaches to baselines, monitoring, and evaluations, is required
Good understanding of Accountability to communities
Good working knowledge of statistical packages (Excel, etc.) is required
Excellent knowledge of ODK database
Expert data handling skills (classification, categorization, tabulation, etc.) and demonstrates diligence in data management
Good knowledge of information presentation techniques (graphing, charting, tabling, etc.) and interpreting them
Good contextual knowledge of the local community and social/cultural constraints, realities, and organizational relationships
Ability to understand, explain, and contextualize MEAL tools

World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) has an exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for a suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the
MEAL Officer
role to be based in
Port Moresby, National Capital District.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Officer for the Economic Empowerment & Resilience projects is responsible for implementing a functional MEAL system for these projects. He/she supports the project team in designing, monitoring, and evaluating Accountability and Learning in all the project’s interventions. Moreover, he/she works with the direct supervisor to coordinate and/or implement project baselines and evaluations, and to implement standardized MEAL processes and tools across all Economic Empowerment & Resilience sector projects at the field level.
1.
Program Design
Support EER MEAL Coordinator as requested in contributing to WVPNG, strategy, sectoral frameworks, overall, MEAL system set-up, and ad-hoc requests.
Support the MEAL Coordinator in leading the proposal development process regarding MEAL input (logframe, budgeting for MEAL activities and staffing, MEAL narrative plan, etc.)
Develop project-specific MEAL frameworks for EER projects in coordination with project staff.
2.
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting
Develop methodologies, sampling plans, and tools for outcome and process monitoring studies, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, FGDs, KIIs, etc.
Plan, lead, and oversee the implementation of outcome monitoring studies for grants such as PIMs/PDMs, midline and endline studies, pre/post-tests, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (coordinate, follow up, and review the outcome monitoring methodology, tools, and reports for grants.
Lead assigned project-specific evaluations and baselines at the field level (development of ToR, selection and short-listing consultants, coordination with the consultant, review of design methodology and tools, review final reports, attend interpretation workshops, etc., if externally led; and conduct data analysis and report writing if internally led)
Implement field-level tasks for the outcome and process monitoring of the project, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, midline and end-line studies, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (training of casual workers, planning field data collection, coordination of data collection, supervising, facilitating, coding tools, developing datasets, data cleaning, analysis, reporting)
Provide support in training project staff and partners on reporting requirements, output level monitoring, and conduct regular training for project staff on data collection and data entry for pre-post-tests.
Conduct ITT verifications of projects in coordination with project staff each month and ensure project-level ITTs are updated with accurate data. Key findings are shared with the project team and management at the program review meetings.
Conduct regular project site visits and monitor partner & direct implementation against quality standards through scheduled visits, data quality audits, and spot checks.
Support the project teams in compiling regular quality project reports, including monthly (Monthly Management Report), Quarterly, mid-year, annual, and end-of-project reports.
Ensure that the project team and other stakeholders discuss and address critical MEAL findings and recommendations.
3
.
Accountability to Children & Communities
Assess community preferences and needs to inform the design of contextually appropriate accountability processes and share outcomes/results with communities, colleagues, and partners.
Implement the project accountability plan/design developed based on the community's preferences for providing information, consulting with communities, promoting participation, and collecting and acting on feedback and complaints.
Receive, process, and respond to feedback and complaints, and communicate progress to the children, communities, and stakeholders.
Implement the plan for sharing information based on community stakeholders' needs and preferences and adjust as needed. Collaborate with colleagues to gather relevant and accurate project information to be shared openly with communities, stakeholders, and partners.
Ensure that all feedback and complaints received from communities are promptly and accurately recorded/updated in the system, and that loops are closed within the timeline.
Sensitize community members about their right to information, consultation, participation, and providing feedback and complaints, while emphasizing their responsibility to support solutions.
Support investigation of allegations of irregularities, fraud, corruption, or other forms of misconduct by directly liaising with the affected communities, according to guidelines, and promptly, promoting trust and safety.
Engage community members in measuring the effectiveness of Accountability practices, providing recommendations for and addressing areas that need improvement in coordination with the accountability core team, and conducting other consultation activities that can support the design of new programmes.
Conduct exit interviews, observation, and reporting.
4. Research and Learning
Co-lead lessons learned events for the project with project managers and technical staff (preparation, facilitation, and report writing). Implement any potential research studies at the field level (data collection, cleaning) - (based on WVPNG strategic priorities for Evidence Building)
5. Miscellaneous
Support WVPNG-wide PQ assignments such as assessments and program design, as assigned by the supervisor.
Attend internal and external meetings relevant to assigned projects
Attend internal and external training, workshops, events, etc.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION
/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Minimum one to two years of experience in working in a relief or development NGO with a focus on MEAL processes
A BA Degree in international development, international relations, public health, nutrition, statistics, community development, project management or other relevant disciplines is required.
Experience in the design and implementation of MEAL systems, including qualitative and quantitative approaches to baselines, monitoring, and evaluations, is required
Good understanding of Accountability to communities
Good working knowledge of statistical packages (Excel, etc.) is required
Excellent knowledge of ODK database
Expert data handling skills (classification, categorization, tabulation, etc.) and demonstrates diligence in data management
Good knowledge of information presentation techniques (graphing, charting, tabling, etc.) and interpreting them
Information dissemination skills are required
Ability to work effectively under pressure
Organization, planning, and time management skills
Detail-oriented and able to verify data quality
Stays open to internal and external feedback
Good contextual knowledge of the local community and social/cultural constraints, realities, and organizational relationships

This is a key leadership role responsible for ensuring all facilities are safe, compliant, efficient, and operating to the highest standards.
The General Manager will oversee multi-site operations, maintenance, engineering, utilities, cleaning, and site services, ensuring these functions align with corporate strategy, HSSEQ standards, sustainability goals, and long-term property development plans.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic & Operational Leadership
Provide strategic direction across all Facilities & Services operations.

Drive performance, service quality, and operational readiness across all sites.
Asset & Maintenance Management

Develop business cases for major projects, upgrades, and asset replacements.
Lead procurement, contractor performance management, and tendering processes.
Establish and enforce SLAs, contracts, and value-for-money outcomes with critical service providers.
HSSEQ, Risk & Compliance
Champion a zero-harm culture and ensure compliance with PNG laws, safety standards, and corporate HSSEQ policies.
Manage operational risks and ensure robust safety, environmental, and quality systems.
Leadership & People Development
Lead, coach, and develop multi-disciplinary teams across multiple sites.
Build a high-performance culture focused on accountability, service excellence, and continuous improvement.
Stakeholder & Project Management

Provide technical input into new developments, refurbishments, and major projects.
Represent Facilities & Services in executive forums and cross-divisional initiatives.

Postgraduate qualification in Business or Project Management (desirable).

Experience
Minimum 10 years’ experience in facilities, engineering, or property operations management.
Proven leadership of multi-site operations and technical teams.
Strong contract management, financial acumen, and asset lifecycle management capability.
Competencies
Strategic and operational planning
Asset and facilities management
Budgeting and financial control
Risk and compliance management
Vendor and contract management
Stakeholder engagement
Performance and change management
Behavioural Attributes
Safety-first mindset with strong operational discipline
Commercially astute, results-focused, and calm under pressure
Clear communicator with strong influencing and relationship-building skills
Hands-on leadership style with a commitment to developing people
High integrity, accountability, and commitment to service excellence
Why Join Us?
This is a high-impact role within one of PNG’s most respected and established companies. You will have the opportunity to shape operational excellence, influence major development projects, and lead a national team delivering essential services across the portfolio.

25268.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
The primary purpose of the role is to implement site safety policy and procedures working under Operational Services by managing the weekly works and maintenance schedule set out by the planners, ensuring work crews and subcontractors working under Operational Services collaborate with other areas and sections to support regarding breakdowns and shutdowns.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Coordinate workshop and site maintenance and refurbishment works.
Give direction, delegate tasks, and provide technical assistance to subordinates.
Implement planned maintenance deadlines.
Check on Purchase Orders and deliveries of materials for site works.
Ensure cost control measures are considered by utilizing resources available to full capacity.
Supervise and check on work crews on daily.
Report any hazards and incidents.
Ensure training requirements are met.
Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings.
Regularly monitor and evaluate staff performance in consultation with Superintendent – Facilities.
Provide coaching for performance improvement.
Subject to management review, takes disciplinary action to address performance deficiencies, in accordance with the Company’s rules and policies.
Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the staff.
Responds to emergency situations as necessary.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Superintendent – Facilities.
Maintain safe work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have Trade Qualifications, preferably Carpentry, Diploma of Building, others will be considered.
Able to use software packages for emails, reporting, file storage, scheduling,
CAD drawing or equivalent desirable.
3 to 5yr Experience in Mining, Construction or other heavy industry
Methods, practices, techniques, and equipment used in the construction, maintenance, and repair of facilities.
Principles and practices of budget preparation and administration.
Safety regulations, safe work practices and safety equipment related to the work.
Principles and practices of effective management and supervision.
Company SOP’s, policies, and regulations.
Plan, assign, direct and coordinate a variety of overlapping work areas.
Select, motivate, and evaluate staff and provide training and development.
Prepare clear and concise records, reports, correspondence, and other written materials.
Exercise independent judgment and initiative within general policy guidelines; establish and maintain effective working relationships with those encountered in the course of the work.
Hold an appropriate trade certificate and must have at least 5 years’ experience in a supervisory capacity, they should also have experience in training of both operating and maintenance personnel.
Must be a self-starter and be very resourceful and of sober habit.
Good health and physical ability are a prerequisite, as is the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Be flexible and adaptable and be a team player.
Good computer skills.
Good oral and written communication skills
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

24700.description:
Summary






The Project Planner / Scheduler is responsible for developing, monitoring, and updating the project schedule across all phases of construction. This role ensures alignment between time, cost, and resource planning to support on-time and on-budget delivery. The position requires close collaboration with engineers, quantity surveyors, and project managers to monitor performance and mitigate delays.


Duties and Responsibilities






1. Pre-Construction Stage




Develop the Master Project Schedule using Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, or similar tools.


Define the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), activity sequences, durations, and dependencies.


Identify project milestones, deliverables, and critical paths for effective tracking.


Support the preparation of manpower, material, and equipment forecasts.


Coordinate with the commercial and cost teams to ensure schedule-cost alignment.


Review cost estimates with quantity surveyors and estimators for scheduling accuracy.




2. Construction Stage




Monitor actual work progress against the baseline schedule and identify variances.


Update schedules regularly based on site conditions, change orders, or revised scopes.


Highlight potential delays and assess their impact on overall project timelines.


Coordinate with project teams to propose recovery plans when needed.


Generate weekly and monthly project progress reports with visual timelines and critical path tracking.




3. Post-Construction Stage




Prepare detailed close-out schedules to support final inspections and commissioning activities.


Analyze and compare planned versus actual performance data to assess overall schedule efficiency.


Develop delay analysis and Extension of Time (EOT) reports with supporting documentation for claims.




4. Final Completion & Handover




Ensure all project planning and scheduling records are updated and properly archived.


Document lessons learned and provide input to improve future scheduling methodologies and project planning processes.




Job Requirements








Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, or a related field.


Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in project planning and scheduling.


Proficient in Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, or other recognized scheduling software.


Solid understanding of construction processes, project phases, and planning principles.


Strong analytical, organizational, and time management skills.


Excellent written and verbal communication skills for preparing reports and coordinating with project stakeholders.


Ability to work independently and collaboratively under pressure in dynamic project environments.


Full-time position based at the project office with regular visits to construction sites.


May require occasional extended hours to meet reporting deadlines or resolve schedule issues.


Work may involve outdoor site inspections in varying weather and environmental conditions.

Summary






The Escort & Emergency Response Team Leader plays a critical role in safeguarding people and property by leading emergency preparedness and patrol coordination. The role ensures efficient incident handling, digital reporting, resource readiness, and secure escort of personnel and sensitive materials. A focus on digital tools, professional conduct, and sustainable practices is key to success in this role.


Duties and Responsibilities








Lead, train, and supervise emergency response and patrol teams during drills and actual incidents.


Escort staff, visitors, VIPs, and sensitive materials securely during emergencies or high-risk situations.


Digitally manage and maintain emergency and patrol equipment (e.g., radios, med kits, evacuation tools).


Coordinate closely with police, fire, medical, and other emergency services as needed.


Implement and regularly review emergency response procedures to ensure safety and efficiency.


Respond promptly to incidents, alarms, and threats; ensure clear action plans for evacuation or containment.


Use digital platforms for incident logging, communication, and shift reporting.


Plan and lead emergency drills, debriefings, and readiness checks with structured follow-ups.


Support sustainability efforts by optimizing resource use, reducing waste, and using energy-conscious tools and methods.




Job Requirements








High School Certificate or Diploma in Security, Safety Management, or related field preferred.


First Aid, CPR, or Basic Life Support (BLS) certified, or willingness to obtain.

Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Senior Training Supervisor
to join our team on a permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 21/14 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Buka, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Vanimo, Wewak or Tabar group of Islands.

Technical accountabilities
Ensuring safe work practices, own health and safety and all other workers by identifying hazards and ensuring issues and risks are reported and addressed.

Providing training governance, guidance, and support for implementation of system/enablers of the training business processes
Liaising with line managers to identify training gaps and develop training need analysis
Contributing to the development of training policies and procedures
Ensuring all certificates issued are in line with the Certificate Issue Guidelines and quality audit register for all departments and contractors
Assisting in the development of monthly reports and the completion of training reports.
Evaluating individual and organizational performance to ensure training is meeting business needs and improving performance
Selecting and managing resources, including working with both internal employees and training vendors to develop and deliver training outcomes
Developing training opportunities between online and on-the-job, coaching, mentoring and other training methods. Identify and implement opportunities
Ensure training/assessment and RPL’s are delivered as per schedule.
Provide administrative support and guidance to the Training Administrator
Schedule accountabilities
Managing effective use of available resources, including own time, in support of the delivery of the HR Training team.
People accountabilities
Contributing to the development of capability within the team/crew.
Contributing to an effective team/crew.
Ensuring own work performance meets all role requirements; and taking appropriate professional development actions.
Ensuring outputs and development of the team/crew.
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​

Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara’s Values

Current unencumbered ‘C’ Class Driver’s Licence

At least five (5) years relevant experience
NTC Registration
High energy with demonstrated capacity to deliver under pressure
Desirable

Program Design
Support MEAL Coordinator as requested (WVPNG, strategy, sectoral frameworks, overall, MEAL system set-up, ad-hoc requests)
Support the MEAL Coordinator in leading the proposal development process regarding MEAL input (logframe, budgeting for MEAL activities and staffing, MEAL narrative plan, etc.)
Develop project-specific MEAL frameworks in coordination with project staff.
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting
Develop methodologies, sampling plans, and tools for outcome and process monitoring studies, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, FGDs, KIIs, etc.
Plan, lead, and oversee the implementation of outcome monitoring studies for grants such as PIMs/PDMs, midline and endline studies, pre/post-tests, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (coordinate, follow up, and review the outcome monitoring methodology, tools, and reports for grants.
Lead BEAN project-specific evaluations and baselines at the field level (development of ToR, selection and short-listing consultants, coordination with the consultant, review of design methodology and tools, review final reports, attend interpretation workshops, etc., if externally led; and conduct data analysis and report writing if internally led)
Implement field-level tasks for the outcome and process monitoring of the project, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, midline and end-line studies, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (training of casual workers, planning field data collection, coordination of data collection, supervising, facilitating, coding tools, developing datasets, data cleaning, analysis, reporting)
Provide support in training project staff and partners on reporting requirements, output level monitoring, and conduct regular training for project staff on data collection and data entry for pre-post-tests.
Conduct ITT verifications of projects in coordination with project staff each month and ensure project-level ITTs are updated with accurate data. Key findings are shared with the project team and management at the program review meetings.
Conduct regular project site visits and monitor partner & direct implementation against quality standards through scheduled visits, data quality audits, and spot checks.
Support the project teams in compiling regular quality BEAN project reports, including monthly (Monthly Management Report), Quarterly, mid-year, annual, and end-of-project reports.
Ensure that the project team and other stakeholders discuss and address critical MEAL findings and recommendations.
Accountability to Children & Communities
Assess community preferences and needs to inform the design of contextually appropriate accountability processes and share outcomes/results with communities, colleagues, and partners.
Implement the BEAN project accountability plan/design developed based on the community's preferences for providing information, consulting with communities, promoting participation, and collecting and acting on feedback and complaints.
Receive, process, and respond to feedback and complaints, and communicate progress to the children, communities, and stakeholders.
Implement the plan for sharing information based on community stakeholders' needs and preferences and adjust as needed. Collaborate with colleagues to gather relevant and accurate project information to be shared openly with communities, stakeholders, and partners.
Ensure that all feedback and complaints received from communities are promptly and accurately recorded/updated in the system, and that loops are closed within the timeline.
Sensitize community members about their right to information, consultation, participation, and providing feedback and complaints, while emphasizing their responsibility to support solutions.
Support investigation of allegations of irregularities, fraud, corruption, or other forms of misconduct by directly liaising with the affected communities, according to guidelines, and promptly, promoting trust and safety.
Engage community members in measuring the effectiveness of Accountability practices, providing recommendations for and addressing areas that need improvement in coordination with the accountability core team, and conducting other consultation activities that can support the design of new programmes.
Conduct exit interviews, observation, and reporting.
Research and Learning
Co-lead lessons learned events for the project with project managers and technical staff (preparation, facilitation, and report writing)
Implement any potential research studies at the field level (data collection, cleaning) - (based on WVPNG strategic priorities for Evidence Building)
Miscellaneous
Support WVPNG-wide PQ assignments such as assessments and program design, as assigned by the supervisor.
Attend internal and external meetings relevant to assigned projects
Attend internal and external training, workshops, events, etc.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
A BA Degree in international development, international relations, public health, nutrition, statistics, community development, or other relevant disciplines is required.
Minimum one to two years of experience in working in a relief or development NGO with a focus on MEAL processes
Experience in the design and implementation of MEAL systems, including qualitative and quantitative approaches to baselines, monitoring, and evaluations, is required
Good understanding of Accountability to communities
Good working knowledge of statistical packages (Excel, etc.) is required
Excellent knowledge of ODK database
Expert data handling skills (classification, categorization, tabulation, etc.) and demonstrates diligence in data management
Good knowledge of information presentation techniques (graphing, charting, tabling, etc.) and interpreting them
Good contextual knowledge of the local community and social/cultural constraints, realities, and organizational relationships
Ability to understand, explain, and contextualize MEAL tools
High-level communications skills
Ability to build positive relationships in a cross-cultural environment
Preferred working knowledge of advanced statistical packages (SPSS, etc.)

Crane Operator
Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Crane Operator
to join our team. permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 15/13 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Buka, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo, or Tabar group of Islands.
(
Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Plant Crane Supervisor, the Crane Operator is responsible for a non - slew crane (franna Mac- 25) and a mobile slew crane (below & above 100 Tonnes) to move, lift and position materials at site.
The opportunity
Ensuring safe work practices, own health and safety and all other workers by identifying hazards and ensuring issues and risks are reported and addressed.
Performing daily pre & post prestart checks.
Understanding load chart and executing the job
Cleaning the maintaining the machine
Operating each specific crane as per OEM standards
Inspecting the crane to ensure its safety.
Set up mobile slew crane as per OEM standards.
Rigging duties as required
Compilation and adherence to JHA’s, SWP, SOP and Lift Plans
Perform routine crane maintenance work such as cleaning and lubricating cranes as required.
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara Values
Minimum grade 10 certificate
Current unrestricted PNG Driver Licence class 7.
Certificate to perform dogging CPCCLDG3001A or RIIHAN208D.
Certificate to operate non- slew (franna) crane TLILIC3006A or RIIHAN212D.
Certificate to operate mobile slew crane up to 100 tonne TLILIC0014 or RIIHAN304D.
Certificate to operate mobile slew crane over 100 tonnes TLILI4011A.
Minimum 5 years industry experience.
Basic knowledge of hydraulic systems on cranes.
Strong ability to work effectively within a team.
Ability to operate and control equipment.
Prepared to work out of hours as required.
Good attention to detail.

Simberi Operations
and to apply for this role, please visit:
https://www.livehire.com/job/stbarbara-png/MRAY9

th

All qualified applicants will be given equal consideration, regardless of their race, national origin, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation or gender identity.
Apply

25324.description:
Marketing Manager
Marketing - Port Moresby, NCD
Role Title: Marketing Manager
Role Type: Senior Level
Department: Marketing
Reports to: The Director – Institutional Development
Location: IBSUniversity & IBS College of TVET
Employment Type: Full-Time
Organizational Context:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its’ humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 38 years. Today we are one of the largest business schools in the country and off degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 12 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.
Our success is the fruits of our dedicated team committed to making a difference in Papua New Guinea, through their efforts to help educate current and futures citizens on Papua New Guinea.
A Career with Us:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.
Job Purpose
The Marketing Manager is responsible for leading and managing all marketing, branding, promotions, recruitment support, call center operations, and stakeholder engagement across IBSUniversity, IBS College of TVET, IBS Centre of Excellence, the Research Division, and the Career Development Centre.
The role drives student enrolments, strengthens the IBS brand, builds strong school and industry partnerships, and ensures coordinated communication across all IBS business arms.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Marketing & Branding
Develop and execute annual marketing strategies aligned with IBS’s goals.
Lead brand positioning and ensure consistent branding across all IBS entities.
Oversee all advertising campaigns, promotional activities, and media engagements.
Conduct market research and track competitor trends to inform strategy.
Student Recruitment Support
Implement comprehensive recruitment campaigns for all programs.
Coordinate closely with the Call Centre, Enrolment Team, and Academic Schools to support lead conversion.
Lead Open Days, Roadshows, Career Fairs, and School Awareness events.
Call Centre Leadership & Customer Engagement
Manage and supervise the Call Centre team to ensure high-quality enquiry handling.
Set call handling standards (speed, tone, conversion approach, follow-ups).
Monitor call logs, response times, lead follow-ups, and enquiry conversion rates.
Develop call scripts, FAQs, and customer service guidelines.
Ensure daily, weekly, and monthly reporting from the Call Centre to track lead generation and conversion performance.
Coach call center staff on customer service excellence and enrolment messaging.
Partnership & MOA Development
Lead MOA signings with secondary schools in NCD, Central, and provincial areas.
Maintain strong relationships with principals, career advisers, and education leaders.
Conduct partner school outreach activities, including workshops and career sessions.
Digital Marketing & Social Media
Oversee social media strategy and content creation (Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube).
Manage online enquiry responses and ensure customer-friendly engagement.
Track digital analytics (leads, reach, engagement, conversion) and improve ROI.
Marketing Team Leadership
Provide direction, coaching, and performance management for all marketing staff and call center officers.
Set monthly KPIs and targets for marketing and call center teams.
Facilitate ongoing training for digital marketing, branding, and customer service skills.
Stakeholder Engagement & Community Relations
Represent IBS in community events, education expos, and corporate networking.
Strengthen IBS visibility through CSR programs and community outreach.
Build productive partnerships with churches, NGOs, businesses, and local leaders.
Support to IBS Business Arms
Deliver tailored marketing and branding support to:
IBSUniversity – academic programs and Schools
IBS College of TVET – certificate & diploma programs
IBS Centre of Excellence – corporate training, workshops & team building
Research Division – publications, conferences & awareness activities
Career Development Centre – student employability, employer partnerships
Reporting & Performance Management
Monthly marketing and call center performance reports.
Maintain updated databases for leads, conversions, partner schools, and industry stakeholders.
Ensure proper use of marketing and call center budgets.
Key Deliverables
Annual Marketing Plan & Budget
Monthly Enrolment Campaigns
Operational Call Centre Dashboard & Conversion Reports
Digital Marketing & Social Media Analytics
Signed MOAs with Secondary Schools
Updated Marketing Collateral
High community visibility and strong stakeholder networks
Qualifications & Experience
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in marketing, Communication, Business, or related field.
Experience: 8 + years of marketing experience including minimum 3 years in a Managerial role and team leadership.
Strong experience in customer service, call center management, or sales.
Demonstrated experience in digital marketing and branding.
Desirable
Experience in education sector marketing.
Knowledge of the PNG education landscape.
Experience in public speaking or community outreach.
Skills & Competencies
Technical Skills
Marketing strategy & execution
Call center operations management
Digital marketing & social media
Event management
Market research & data interpretation
Stakeholder engagement
Soft Skills
Excellent communication and customer service
Leadership and people management
Creative problem-solving
Cultural awareness
Strong organizational ability
Personal Attributes
Confident, professional, and people-oriented
High integrity and work ethic
Passionate about youth development and education
Adaptable and able to travel as required
Committed ambassador of the IBS brand
Apply

Monier Limited, the single largest producer, supplier and distributer of construction materials and building products in PNG is seeking to recruit a suitably qualified and highly motivated individual for the following position:
Human Resource Manager
To assist the Management in providing Human Resources advises and directions in line with Policy in all HR matters including; Selection & recruitment, induction of new employees, industrial and employee relations, employee development, training, review and formulation of HR Policies, Organizational Structures, development and management of performance management systems, Remuneration & Benefits, headcount management, leave liabilities reports, review of salary structure, HR Admin and payroll related duties.

Manage employee & industrial relations, recruitment and induction of new employees within context of established HR processes and in consultation with respective departmental Managers and Supervisors.

5 – 7 years’ experience in all areas of Human Resources including Labour & Employee Relations.

25190.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
The Permit to Work (PTW) Supervisor is a part of the Processing Department who leads and guides the permit to work team to ensure the energy control & isolations and permits to work are completed to a standard that ensures that safety, environmental, and operational risks are maintained at an impeccable standard for those relying upon them to safely complete their work.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Provide leadership, coaching and mentoring to a team of Permit Issuers in their role to ensure the PTW system is being followed, eliminating exposure to risks while workers are carrying out work.
Identify and carry out safe and effective isolations in the field to ensure the safety of all personnel who are required to perform work on the equipment.  Confirm IRS documents are correct and relevant to the job to be performed.  Create new IRS documents as required.
Verify that all necessary safety procedures and controls are in place before issuing any permit. This includes confirming of risk assessments, JSEAs, and required personal protective equipment (PPE).
Take part in shutdown planning meetings, prepare IRS documents in line with shutdown plan and work lists, ensuring they are prepared for issue in line with the shutdown schedule.
Perform isolations as per the shutdown schedule, prepare permit control boards and issue permits to those performing the work. Deisolate and return the plant to operating condition as jobs are completed on equipment items.
Work closely with supervisors and safety personnel to ensure that all isolation safety precautions are understood and implemented. Provide clear guidance to workers regarding the requirements outlined in the permit, emphasising safety and emergency procedures. Notify relevant stakeholders of any changes to work conditions or permits and ensure that any new permits or revised permits are issued promptly.
Before issuing a permit, review permit receiver’s JSEA and other related documents and ensure the documents are in line with the task. Ensure compliance with established isolation and permit practices, ensuring that all personnel involved in the work are adhering to safety regulations.
Maintain filing system where all completed and returned permits are scanned into the correct folders on the K92 Processing storage. Keep accurate and up-to-date records of all issued permits, including work details, personnel involved, safety precautions, and any changes made during the work process. Report any violations of safety protocols or non-compliance with issued permits to relevant supervisors or management. Ensure that records are complete and readily available for internal and external audits, ensuring compliance with safety regulations and standards.
Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Coordinator Processing
Utilising available resources, maintain equipment to a safe and efficient standard in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Cost control.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will have some or all the following.
High school diploma or equivalent. Technical diploma or higher in engineering, such as Processing, Mechanical or Electrical, or a related field is preferred
Certification in Occupational Health and Safety, First Aid, or a relevant PTW certification is highly recommended.
Familiarity with HSE Systems: Experience with Health, Safety, and Environmental management systems and regulations (e.g., OSHA, ISO 45001, etc.).
At least 3 years of PTW experience working in minerals Processing, Oil & Gas, construction, or maintenance environments, with a specific focus on safety management.
Have worked in the mineral processing or oil and gas industry in a similar role for at least 5 years.
Proactive and able to maintain continuous improvement of the PTW system.
Proven ability to lead a team of permit issuers
Ability to maintain the high-level standards required by a PTW team and infrastructure, equipment and tooling.
Exceptional planning and execution skills
Clear understanding of P&ID and PFD drawings
Demonstrated ability to lead a team in Energy control and isolation systems
Demonstrated ability to lead a team to maintain PTW activities including for high-risk tasks.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of Safety, environmental systems, procedures and standards
Demonstrated ability to work with planning and scheduling teams, for preparing isolations and permits for plant shutdowns
Experience with gas testing equipment control, care, servicing and testing.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

25391.description:
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The purpose of this position is to ensure that someone is responsible for ensuring and maintaining stock levels of TB and HIV drugs and medical supplies at all levels at the region, ensuring constant supply of drugs and laboratory commodities, ensuring TBHIV Drug Quality Assurance (QA) through ensuring proper storage condition and warehouse practices and assist the National PSM Coordinator in providing the necessary trainings and updating the guidelines for PSM support for the NTP & HIV Programs. The Regional PSM Coordinator will be deployed to the Area Medical Store (AMS), Badili. He/She will work closely with NPSMC, NDoH (MSPD, PSSB, NTP, HIV Programs), Provincial Health Authorities, TB Basic Management Unit Sites (BMUs), ART sites and donor partners.
MAJOR ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
Ensure the supply chain for TB and HIV commodities including TBHIV Lab commodities are consistent and available at all times
.
Effective communication with partners and stakeholders (TB/HIV Programs, MSPD,CPHL, PSSB,WHO, PHA/PHO and ART sites)
Forecast demand for drugs whilst monitoring stock levels for respective facilities, provinces.
Coordinate with CPHL and Provinces on Lab commodities requirement for distribution.
Ensure stock inventory is available and maintained in respective provinces and facility level in the form of stock card and msupply,
Execute quarterly/ monthly distribution of TB & HIV drugs plus buffer stocks. This includes stock data review and calculation of Current stock availability verses the consumption and issuance data from respective TB/HIV Sites. This includes Lab commodities for TB/HIV
Conduct monthly monitoring of provincial and facility stocks for both TB & HIV commodities.
Conduct Quarterly stock take of both TB & HIV commodities at Badili, AMS.
Removal of Expired Stocks in warehouse, making adjustment to mSupply accordingly
Utilize, maintaining and updating mSupply for managing TB/HIV commodities (inventory, stock take, distribution and procurement).
Overseeing the movement of incoming and outgoing shipment (Including Covid-19 procurement under GF) from AMS badili to TB/HIV sites and Covid station.
Provide technical assistance to store man/Gov logistics staff at AMS Badili and health facility personnel at provincial level.
Conduct regular (quarterly) supervisory visits to provinces for monitoring and provision of technical assistance in management of TB & HIV commodities
Ensure Quality Assurance for TB/HIV Drugs
Maintain good storage condition & area conducive for TB & HIV drugs at AMS ensuring proper warehousing, storage and distribution practices is implemented and maintained.
Conduct drug sampling activity whenever required for QC testing
Ensuring and Maintaining quality throughout the logistics process.
Ensure all operations for PSM related administrative and technical activities are in place.
Maintain appropriate filing systems to ensure information on all areas of implementation, as well as transactions, are readily available.
Ensure security protocols and procedures are followed in the day to day operation of National office.
Maintain an activity log, recording details of field visits.
Prepare and provide quality and comprehensive Supervisory visit report.
Prepare and provide monthly progress reports to NPSMC Coordinator.
Undertake all program related activities as directed by the National TB & HIV program.
Develop and maintain good working relationships with the project partners, sub recipients, and key stakeholders including LFA
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Degree in Pharmacy and or PSM degree or similar
Knowledge of pharmaceutical warehouse management, drug management, inventory, procurement & supply as well as drug logistics.
Should have excellent organization, communication and interpersonal skills
Team player and capacity to deliver the services in constricted timeframes.
Experience in the usage of computers and officer software packages (MS Word, Excel, Power Point)
3 years’ work experience in o Pharmacy field or similar.
Physically fit with no underlying medical conditions.
Good communication skills in written and spoken English
The position requires might require traveling to the Area program
Be available to work weekends and on short notice.

Known for high professional standards, responsible management and steady growth, the organisation offers a supportive, well-governed environment with genuine career development opportunities.
About the Role
As the Finance Business Partner – Properties, you will be responsible for overseeing all finance operations for the Properties Division while contributing to strategic decision-making across the portfolio. Based in Port Moresby and reporting directly to the Group CFO, you will manage financial performance, ensure regulatory compliance, and lead a small team across finance and administration.
This is a hands-on senior role requiring strong financial expertise, organisational capability, and the confidence to partner with senior leadership.
Key Responsibilities
Oversee the preparation of financial statements, including P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reports
Lead budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis and financial planning
Monitor financial performance and recommend corrective actions
Ensure compliance with tax legislation, financial regulations and internal policies
Manage accounts payable, accounts receivable and payroll processes
Support audit preparation and maintain strong internal controls
Lead, manage and mentor finance and administration staff
Work closely with the Group CFO and property leaders on strategic and operational decisions
Qualifications, Skills & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance with a professional certification, CPA or CMA is an advantage
Minimum 5+ years’ experience in financial management, having led a team
Strong knowledge of accounting principles, compliance requirements and financial regulations
Experience in budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting, preferably in
property, real estate, or asset management.
Systems experience with QuickBooks, SAP or similar platforms
Working knowledge of PNG statutory requirements (taxation, superannuation, labour, workers’ compensation, etc.)
Strong leadership capability with excellent communication, analytical and organisational skills.
To apply for this position, interested candidates are asked to submit:
A cover letter addressing key criteria of the role
An updated CV in Microsoft Word format, outlining employment history, educational qualifications, and listing three referees (referees will only be contacted if shortlisted)
